title: The Trans-Planckian Problem
bottleneck: Inflation stretches quantum fluctuations from sub-Planckian scales to observable ones, meaning CMB predictions depend on physics at energies where quantum gravity should dominate but is unknown. Proposed resolutions (modified dispersion, bouncing pre-histories) are speculative, and the standard calculation simply assumes unknown physics decouples. Some argue that unknown Planck-scale physics naturally decouples, making the problem moot, but this is an assumption rather than a result.
why_it_blocks: This is cosmology's quiet foundational gamble: its best-tested early-universe theory rests on an unjustified extrapolation across the Planck scale.
current_state: The problem is acknowledged but unresolved; it motivates searches for trans-Planckian signatures in non-Gaussianity, none found so far. The debate matters because it determines whether inflationary predictions are robust or rest on uncontrolled extrapolation.
